Subject: Performance SLO: p95/p99 latency - hosted API vs current provider (post-call recap & next steps)

Thanks again for the call earlier — great conversation. Quick recap of the performance/SLO items we covered and the proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of FinLytics targets (from call):
- End-to-end p95 <= 250 ms
- End-to-end p99 <= 500 ms
- Sustained concurrency: 50 concurrent inference sessions
- Typical payload: 350 tokens avg (mostly short summaries + metadata)
- Streaming: important for chat UX; must support chunked token streaming with ~100ms server-side frame intervals

Current provider numbers you shared (approx):
- p95 ~ 420 ms, p99 ~ 1.1 s (end-to-end including networking + app layer)

Redwood hosted API baseline (what we typically see for similar workloads):
- p95 ~ 160-200 ms, p99 ~ 350-420 ms (varies by sequence length + batching)
- Streaming supported end-to-end (we surface tokens as they're generated)

Action items / next steps:
1) FinLytics -> share a small sample of production traffic (anonymized) and a short token distribution (we discussed ~10k calls). Include example request/response pairs + expected concurrency pattern.
2) Redwood -> run a targeted perf window against both hosted API and a current-provider-like config; we'll generate a latency matrix (p50/p95/p99) and streaming latencies. Expected deliverable: latency matrix + raw logs + test harness config.
3) Schedule a 2-hour perf window next week; please indicate preferred times (we recommended Wed/Thu morning PT).
4) Documentation: attached a short matrix and the test plan outline.

Attachments: finlytics_p95_p99_test_results.pdf (stub), redwood-hosted-vs-currentprovider-latency-matrix.xlsx (stub)

If that aligns, I'll start the perf schedule and loop in our infra team.

—Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this looks good. A couple clarifications from our side: 
- The p95/p99 targets I quoted are end-to-end from our webapp to inference and back; the 350 tokens avg is a good estimate.
- Streaming is required for our chat UI (we do progressive rendering). We care about both the token-level arrival time and the first-token latency.
- We can provide a 10k-sample anonymized payload plus a small script to replay at desired concurrency. I'll drop those files into the Drive link you shared by EOD Monday.

Do you need any special headers or auth test tokens to replicate our real-world network path?

—Alex

Perfect — thanks Alex. For the perf run we'll need: 
- Anonymized payloads (10k samples) and an indication of request size/token counts
- Replay script or description of pacing (ramp, sustained, burst patterns)
- Preferred perf window times (Wed/Thu mornings PT work for us)
- Any special auth headers (a short-lived test token is fine)

We'll do two passes in the perf window: 
A) Hosted API baseline at your expected concurrency (50 sustained, with 100-concurrency bursts)
B) Provider-like baseline: run a config that approximates your current provider (same model family + quantization settings) so we can compare apples-to-apples.

Deliverables from our side after the window: 
- p50/p95/p99 latency matrix (end-to-end), streaming token arrival distribution, and concurrency scaling graph.
- Raw request/response logs (anonymized) and the test harness config.

I'll attach the matrix and the planned test harness. If that works, I'll lock in Wed 9:00–11:00 PT next week.

Attachments: redwood-hosted-vs-currentprovider-latency-matrix.xlsx (stub)

—Marissa

Laura/Aditya — forwarding the thread from FinLytics. Key asks: 10k-sample replay, target concurrency 50 sustained / 100 burst, streaming must be validated (first-token and per-token arrival). Can you confirm the following on our side before Wed 9am PT: 
- Test harness ready and able to run both hosted and provider-like configs?
- We have a set of test tokens and a network path that approximates FinLytics (they will provide a short-lived test token and replay script).
- Can we capture both end-to-end and server-side-only latencies so we can isolate network variability?

Also note FinLytics cares about p95 <=250ms and p99 <=500ms. Our hosted baseline is promising but let's ensure we capture streaming frames (they want ~100ms frame intervals).

Thanks — I'll schedule the perf window tentatively and update when FinLytics confirms the Drive upload.

—Marissa
